svg.text: Testing a spread instead of a center
Exam scores: the department says σ = 8.6. A professor thinks the spread is smaller. Sample: n = 20, s = 6.9.
the question is about σ, not μ
2. If σ really is 8.6, how small can s get?
where s lands across many samples of 20 if H0 is true
If H0 is true, s² / σ0² is close to 1, so χ² is close to df = 19. Ours is 6.9² / 8.6² = 0.64, giving 12.23.
That is lower than usual, but s would have to be below 6.28 (χ² below 10.117) to land in the lowest 5%.
